requirement:
The instructions supplied under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions` tell the agent to call `finish_search` for every delivered
page before submitting its answer. They explain how to select the tags of
excerpts used as evidence and how to pass `used: []` when none contributed.
Finishing a page records the selected inputs without fetching more source.
rationale:
The subject requires the first-search `instructions` to say four things. The test `src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]` covers each one.

The test takes the `instructions` string from the first delivered result, an empty `search_text` for "absent". It asserts that the string contains these phrases:
- **Call `finish_search` for every delivered page before submitting.** The phrases "Before submitting, close every delivered search page" and "finish_search" cover this.
- **Select the tags of excerpts used as evidence.** The phrase "tags for excerpts you relied on without a separate source read" covers this.
- **Pass `used: []` when none contributed.** The phrase "used:[] if none qualify, including an empty result" covers this.
- **Finishing records inputs without fetching more source.** The phrase "without reading more source" covers this.

The test also checks that a different first search, a `search_structure` call in a fresh session, returns the identical instructions string. The structural search therefore carries the same content.

The test additionally checks that later results and continuation pages omit the field. That belongs to the parent requirement `requirements.sdk.graph.search.first_search.instructions`, not to this content requirement.

The assertions are on required substrings, not the full text. This is reasonable, because the requirement states what the instructions must convey, not their exact wording. The test would fail if any of the four elements were removed.

The weakest point is the "records the selected inputs" half of the last element. The phrase "without reading more source" does not assert it directly. The surrounding "tags for excerpts you relied on" phrase and the `finish_search` dependency assertions cover the recording behavior itself. I did not treat this as a gap.

searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
